<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This is the DSpark half of the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash specialized decode on GB300 (#61868). With `decode_backend` set to `latency_specialized`, the DSpark draft layers now run on the same decode executor as the target model, on its fused all-reduce + mHC kernel, attention and routed-expert GEMMs. The draft also samples through the model's `sample_sequential` hook: the fused Markov loop from #64442, plus a Markov chain sharded by vocabulary over the TP ranks at small batches.

Everything is under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`, with its tests. The speculators, the model runner and the other shared code are unchanged. With the switch off, nothing changes.

## Claims

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4) with DSpark (5 draft tokens), the switch on in both arms, this PR against `main`:
- Decode step: −5.1% at batch 1 and −2.5% at batch 8; unchanged at batch 40.
- GSM8K accuracy and the DSpark acceptance length are unchanged, within the spread of repeated runs.

## Validation

### Correctness

GSM8K, all 1,319 questions at concurrency 8, on `main` `866bccf0` and this PR's head merged onto it:

| Task | `main` | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, strict match | 0.976 | 0.971 |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | 4.00 | 3.96 |

Both differences are inside the spread of repeated runs of this PR and #61868 across the earlier revisions: 0.970 to 0.976 for GSM8K, and 3.90 to 3.99 for the acceptance length. The batches, and with them the generated text, differ from run to run.

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

```bash
# One SM100-family GPU: the sharded Markov chain (one rank) bitwise against the
# speculator's eager loop, eagerly and replayed from a CUDA graph
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py -v
# One GPU: #64442's fused Markov loop, which the switch now turns on
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_fused_markov.py -v
# Four GPUs: the TP4 numerics
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v
# Four GB300: five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v
```

| Check | What it covers | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kernel tests (one GB300) | The sharded chain (one rank) bitwise against the speculator's eager loop: temperatures 0, 1 and 0.6, a padding row, BF16 and FP32 logits, eagerly and replayed from a CUDA graph. The draft's routed-expert finalize bitwise against FlashInfer's. | 89 passed, 3 failed. The same 3 fail on `main` (87 passed, 3 failed), in tests this PR does not touch: `test_routed_experts_match_flashinfer[5-graph]` (FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 changed a summation order) and both `test_engram_wkv_prefetch_matches_inline` cases (a test stub lacks `params_dtype`). #63921 fixes both. |
| Fused Markov loop (one GB300) | #64442's test | 2 passed |
| Numerics (TP4) | #61868's collectives | Passed |
| Layers test (4× GB300) | With the switch on, the target's and the draft's executors both run, the draft's layers take the executor's routed-expert GEMMs, its logits come from the executor's LM head, and its `sample_sequential` is the sharded chain over the fused loop. With the switch off, neither executor runs and the draft has no `sample_sequential`. | Passed |
| pre-commit | All hooks | Passes on every changed file |

**CI.** The kernel tests run in the nightly 4×B200 step that #61868 added. No CI agent has four GB300, so the layers test skips there; the draft executor and the sharded chain's cross-rank exchange were validated on GB300 outside CI.

</details>

### Performance

**Decode step.** The speculative step with its draft, timed from the client over long-context decodes: one 524K-token request at batch 1, eight of 84K to 648K tokens at batch 8, and five times those eight at batch 40, with 3,000 output tokens each. The runs are ABBA blocks on one GB300 tray, with one server per block and two repeats per batch size. They compare `main` `866bccf0` with this PR merged onto it, with the switch on in both. Both arms share one FlashInfer autotune cache, so they run the same GEMM tactics.

| Batch | `main` (µs) | This PR (µs) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4,276 | 4,057 | −5.1% |
| 8 | 8,915 | 8,692 | −2.5% |
| 40 | 16,703 | 16,626 | −0.5% |

At batches 1 and 8, every block of this PR beats every block of `main`. At batch 40, the blocks overlap.

**Sharded chain.** The same ABBA on a second tray compares this PR with and without the sharded chain. Without it, the fused loop samples at every batch size.

| Batch | Without (µs) | With (µs) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4,109 | 4,061 | −1.2% |
| 8 | 8,873 | 8,880 | +0.1% |
| 40 | 16,703 | 16,565 | −0.8% |

The chain runs only up to 8 request rows, so the batch-40 difference is noise between blocks. The chain saves about 50 µs per step at batch 1 and nothing measurable at batch 8. It is 1,565 of this PR's 2,475 added lines, all in `specialized_decode/sampling/`. If reviewers prefer the smaller diff, it can be dropped without touching the rest.

## Details

### What changed

All paths are under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`.

| Area | Files | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft executor | `specialized_decode/runtime/draft.py` (new), `runtime/decode.py`, `runtime/model_state.py`, `runtime/warmup.py`, `specialized_decode/__init__.py` | `DraftDecode` runs the DSpark draft layers through the target executor's attention, MoE and boundary steps, on its fused all-reduce + mHC kernel, mailbox, publishing `wo_b` GEMM and mHC side stream. The target's model state builds it after the target's executor and warms both up. |
| Per-layer steps | `attention/step.py`, `moe/step.py`, `boundary/boundary.py`, `boundary/publishing_gemm.py` | Parameters for the draft's layers: the first layer's mHC pre over the expanded embedding, `wo_b` and the MoE kept TP-partial for the next boundary (the draft's stock layers reduce them themselves), and a residual-only last boundary. |
| Routed experts | `moe/routed_expert_finalize_cute.py` (new), `moe/routed_expert_gemm.py` | The draft's top-k finalize after the low-batch GEMMs, in CuTe DSL (adapted from FlashInfer's `finalizeKernel`). |
| Draft model | `dspark.py` | With the switch on, the draft registers for an executor, runs its decode steps on it, and samples through `sample_sequential`: #64442's fused loop, wrapped by the sharded chain once the executor exists. |
| Sharded Markov chain | `specialized_decode/sampling/sharded_markov.py`, `sharded_markov_cute.py` (new) | The draft's Markov chain sharded by vocabulary over the TP ranks, for batches of up to 8 request rows (4 at 8 ranks). |
| Tests | `tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/` | The sharded chain against the eager loop, the finalize kernel, and the draft executor in the layers test. |

### Design notes

**Structure.** The DSpark draft model registers itself when it is built with the switch on. The target's model state from #61868 then builds the draft's executor right after the target's, on the same fused kernel, mailbox and mHC side stream, and the draft model's forward asks it for a step the same way (`plan()`, then `run()`). Once the executor is built, the draft model replaces its `sample_sequential` (#64442's `FusedMarkovSampler`, which the switch implies) with one that sends batches of up to 8 request rows to the sharded chain and the others to the fused loop. `DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential` already asks that hook first, so the speculator is unchanged.

**Sharded chain: rank lockstep.**
- The chain exchanges each position's winner between ranks through a symmetric-memory mailbox, a cross-rank spin inside the draft step and its FULL graph, so every rank must launch it the same number of times.
- Whether it is installed depends only on configuration, and CPU all-reduces at load make the ranks agree on it.
- The per-call choice depends only on the padded batch shape. It applies up to 8 request rows (4 at 8 ranks).
- Steady state reads nothing back from the GPU.
- The draws reproduce the speculator's `gumbel_sample` loop, except for the bias reduction order before its BF16 rounding, so a bias element can differ from cuBLAS's in its last bit. The fused loop above 8 rows draws by inverse CDF (#64442); both sample the cached draft distribution exactly.

## Changelog

- 10-15: First version, stacked on #61868. The draft layers then moved into a draft executor, following #61867.
- 10-17: The draft finalize and the sharded Markov chain ported from run-time-compiled CUDA to CuTe DSL, with bitwise-identical outputs. Rebased onto `main` `03ee2e13` (FlashInfer 0.7.2).
- 10-19 and 10-20: Rebased onto `main` `aa3564ce` and `3b518982`.
- 10-21: #61868 merged; `main` merged into this branch.
- 11-03: Following review, dropped every change outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`: the post-forward CUDA graph, the context side stream, the multi-group DFlash prepare and the generic fused Markov sampler. The draft now samples through the existing `sample_sequential` hook, on #64442's fused loop, and the sharded chain moved to `specialized_decode/sampling/`. Merged `main` `866bccf0` (the measurements above), then `1fc9d008`.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""DSpark's sequential Markov sampling for a small batch, in CuTe DSL.
+
+The kernel samples up to 8 request rows, with the Markov head sharded by
+vocabulary across the tensor-parallel ranks (``sharded_markov.py`` explains the
+design). It is compiled for a number of draft positions ``steps`` (1..8) and
+the element types of the base logits and of the draft-logits cache (BF16 or
+FP32).
+
+For request ``r``, step ``i`` needs r's previous token ``p`` (its anchor for
+``i = 0``)::
+
+    logits_ri = cache_round(base_ri + bf16(markov_head . markov_embed[p]))
+    d_r,i+1   = argmax(logits_ri)                     (temperature 0)
+              = argmax(logits_ri / T_r + gumbel_ri)   (otherwise)
+
+Each rank owns rows ``[rank * V/world, (rank + 1) * V/world)`` of the head.
+Each warp keeps one 16-row tile of that shard in registers for all steps, so
+the head is read once per launch; the ``m16n8k16`` MMA's eight columns carry the
+eight request rows' embeddings, so every row's bias comes from the same MMAs.
+A step is those MMAs, a CTA reduction and a two-level exchange of 64-bit
+candidate keys per request row: the CTAs of a rank fold their best key into a
+rank-local maximum, the last CTA to arrive stores that key, tagged with the
+launch epoch, into every rank's mailbox, and every CTA waits for the ``world``
+records of each row in its own mailbox and takes their maximum. The exchange is
+the grid barrier and the cross-rank argmax at once, so the grid must be
+co-resident: the kernel is launched cooperatively, and its 512-thread
+requirement keeps one CTA per SM within the register file.
+
+The base logits may hold the full vocabulary or only this rank's shard (the
+draft LM head's output before its all-gather): ``base_column`` is the column of
+this rank's first vocabulary entry in them, ``rank * V/world`` or 0.
+
+Rows whose request-state index is negative (CUDA-graph padding) are inert, as
+in the fused path: their tokens are drawn greedily and their logits are not
+cached.
+
+The draft-logits cache must hold the full vocabulary on every rank. Each rank
+writes its shard into its own cache and into a staging buffer of every peer;
+after the last exchange each rank copies the peers' shards from its staging
+buffer into its cache. Staging and mailbox records alternate between two
+parities so that a launch never overwrites what a peer may still be reading
+from the previous launch.
+
+Peer buffer layout (bytes): mailbox records u64
+``[parity 2][step 8][row 8][source rank 8]`` (8 KiB), then the staging logits
+``[parity 2][max_rows][steps][vocab]`` of the cache type at ``STAGING_OFFSET``.
+Local control words (uint32): combine maxima u64 ``[step 8][row 8]`` at words
+0..127, arrivals ``[step 8]`` at 128..135, launches at 136, end arrivals at 137.
+
+Global memory is addressed with 64-bit integers and accessed with explicit PTX,
+so that each access has the state space, cache operator and memory ordering
+the protocol needs (relaxed system-scope mailbox records, L2-only staging
+reads, non-coherent reads of the weights).
+"""

+from cutlass.cutlass_dsl import T, dsl_user_op
+

+              = argmax(logits_ri / T_r + gumbel_ri)   (otherwise)
+
+Each rank owns rows ``[rank * V/world, (rank + 1) * V/world)`` of the head.
+Each warp keeps one 16-row tile of that shard in registers for all steps, so
+the head is read once per launch; the ``m16n8k16`` MMA's eight columns carry the
+eight request rows' embeddings, so every row's bias comes from the same MMAs.
+A step is those MMAs, a CTA reduction and a two-level exchange of 64-bit
+candidate keys per request row: the CTAs of a rank fold their best key into a
+rank-local maximum, the last CTA to arrive stores that key, tagged with the
+launch epoch, into every rank's mailbox, and every CTA waits for the ``world``
+records of each row in its own mailbox and takes their maximum. The exchange is
+the grid barrier and the cross-rank argmax at once, so the grid must be
+co-resident: the kernel is launched cooperatively, and its 512-thread
+requirement keeps one CTA per SM within the register file.
+
+The base logits may hold the full vocabulary or only this rank's shard (the
+draft LM head's output before its all-gather): ``base_column`` is the column of
+this rank's first vocabulary entry in them, ``rank * V/world`` or 0.
+
+Rows whose request-state index is negative (CUDA-graph padding) are inert, as
+in the fused path: their tokens are drawn greedily and their logits are not
+cached.
+
+The draft-logits cache must hold the full vocabulary on every rank. Each rank
+writes its shard into its own cache and into a staging buffer of every peer;
+after the last exchange each rank copies the peers' shards from its staging
+buffer into its cache. Staging and mailbox records alternate between two
+parities so that a launch never overwrites what a peer may still be reading
+from the previous launch.
+
+Peer buffer layout (bytes): mailbox records u64
+``[parity 2][step 8][row 8][source rank 8]`` (8 KiB), then the staging logits
+``[parity 2][max_rows][steps][vocab]`` of the cache type at ``STAGING_OFFSET``.
+Local control words (uint32): combine maxima u64 ``[step 8][row 8]`` at words
+0..127, arrivals ``[step 8]`` at 128..135, launches at 136, end arrivals at 137.
+
+Global memory is addressed with 64-bit integers and accessed with explicit PTX,
+so that each access has the state space, cache operator and memory ordering
+the protocol needs (relaxed system-scope mailbox records, L2-only staging
+reads, non-coherent reads of the weights).
+"""
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda

+import cutlass.cute as cute

+from cutlass.cutlass_dsl import T, dsl_user_op

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This is the DSpark half of the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash specialized decode on GB300 (#61868). With `decode_backend` set to `latency_specialized`, the DSpark draft layers now run on the same decode executor as the target model, on its fused all-reduce + mHC kernel, attention and routed-expert GEMMs. The draft also samples through the model's `sample_sequential` hook: the fused Markov loop from #64442, plus a Markov chain sharded by vocabulary over the TP ranks at small batches.

Everything is under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`, with its tests. The speculators, the model runner and the other shared code are unchanged. With the switch off, nothing changes.

## Claims

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4) with DSpark (5 draft tokens), the switch on in both arms, this PR against `main`:
- Decode step: −5.1% at batch 1 and −2.5% at batch 8; unchanged at batch 40.
- GSM8K accuracy and the DSpark acceptance length are unchanged, within the spread of repeated runs.

## Validation

### Correctness

GSM8K, all 1,319 questions at concurrency 8, on `main` `866bccf0` and this PR's head merged onto it:

| Task | `main` | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, strict match | 0.976 | 0.971 |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | 4.00 | 3.96 |

Both differences are inside the spread of repeated runs of this PR and #61868 across the earlier revisions: 0.970 to 0.976 for GSM8K, and 3.90 to 3.99 for the acceptance length. The batches, and with them the generated text, differ from run to run.

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

```bash
# One SM100-family GPU: the sharded Markov chain (one rank) bitwise against the
# speculator's eager loop, eagerly and replayed from a CUDA graph
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py -v
# One GPU: #64442's fused Markov loop, which the switch now turns on
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_fused_markov.py -v
# Four GPUs: the TP4 numerics
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v
# Four GB300: five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v
```

| Check | What it covers | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kernel tests (one GB300) | The sharded chain (one rank) bitwise against the speculator's eager loop: temperatures 0, 1 and 0.6, a padding row, BF16 and FP32 logits, eagerly and replayed from a CUDA graph. The draft's routed-expert finalize bitwise against FlashInfer's. | 89 passed, 3 failed. The same 3 fail on `main` (87 passed, 3 failed), in tests this PR does not touch: `test_routed_experts_match_flashinfer[5-graph]` (FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 changed a summation order) and both `test_engram_wkv_prefetch_matches_inline` cases (a test stub lacks `params_dtype`). #63921 fixes both. |
| Fused Markov loop (one GB300) | #64442's test | 2 passed |
| Numerics (TP4) | #61868's collectives | Passed |
| Layers test (4× GB300) | With the switch on, the target's and the draft's executors both run, the draft's layers take the executor's routed-expert GEMMs, its logits come from the executor's LM head, and its `sample_sequential` is the sharded chain over the fused loop. With the switch off, neither executor runs and the draft has no `sample_sequential`. | Passed |
| pre-commit | All hooks | Passes on every changed file |

**CI.** The kernel tests run in the nightly 4×B200 step that #61868 added. No CI agent has four GB300, so the layers test skips there; the draft executor and the sharded chain's cross-rank exchange were validated on GB300 outside CI.

</details>

### Performance

**Decode step.** The speculative step with its draft, timed from the client over long-context decodes: one 524K-token request at batch 1, eight of 84K to 648K tokens at batch 8, and five times those eight at batch 40, with 3,000 output tokens each. The runs are ABBA blocks on one GB300 tray, with one server per block and two repeats per batch size. They compare `main` `866bccf0` with this PR merged onto it, with the switch on in both. Both arms share one FlashInfer autotune cache, so they run the same GEMM tactics.

| Batch | `main` (µs) | This PR (µs) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4,276 | 4,057 | −5.1% |
| 8 | 8,915 | 8,692 | −2.5% |
| 40 | 16,703 | 16,626 | −0.5% |

At batches 1 and 8, every block of this PR beats every block of `main`. At batch 40, the blocks overlap.

**Sharded chain.** The same ABBA on a second tray compares this PR with and without the sharded chain. Without it, the fused loop samples at every batch size.

| Batch | Without (µs) | With (µs) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4,109 | 4,061 | −1.2% |
| 8 | 8,873 | 8,880 | +0.1% |
| 40 | 16,703 | 16,565 | −0.8% |

The chain runs only up to 8 request rows, so the batch-40 difference is noise between blocks. The chain saves about 50 µs per step at batch 1 and nothing measurable at batch 8. It is 1,565 of this PR's 2,475 added lines, all in `specialized_decode/sampling/`. If reviewers prefer the smaller diff, it can be dropped without touching the rest.

## Details

### What changed

All paths are under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`.

| Area | Files | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft executor | `specialized_decode/runtime/draft.py` (new), `runtime/decode.py`, `runtime/model_state.py`, `runtime/warmup.py`, `specialized_decode/__init__.py` | `DraftDecode` runs the DSpark draft layers through the target executor's attention, MoE and boundary steps, on its fused all-reduce + mHC kernel, mailbox, publishing `wo_b` GEMM and mHC side stream. The target's model state builds it after the target's executor and warms both up. |
| Per-layer steps | `attention/step.py`, `moe/step.py`, `boundary/boundary.py`, `boundary/publishing_gemm.py` | Parameters for the draft's layers: the first layer's mHC pre over the expanded embedding, `wo_b` and the MoE kept TP-partial for the next boundary (the draft's stock layers reduce them themselves), and a residual-only last boundary. |
| Routed experts | `moe/routed_expert_finalize_cute.py` (new), `moe/routed_expert_gemm.py` | The draft's top-k finalize after the low-batch GEMMs, in CuTe DSL (adapted from FlashInfer's `finalizeKernel`). |
| Draft model | `dspark.py` | With the switch on, the draft registers for an executor, runs its decode steps on it, and samples through `sample_sequential`: #64442's fused loop, wrapped by the sharded chain once the executor exists. |
| Sharded Markov chain | `specialized_decode/sampling/sharded_markov.py`, `sharded_markov_cute.py` (new) | The draft's Markov chain sharded by vocabulary over the TP ranks, for batches of up to 8 request rows (4 at 8 ranks). |
| Tests | `tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/` | The sharded chain against the eager loop, the finalize kernel, and the draft executor in the layers test. |

### Design notes

**Structure.** The DSpark draft model registers itself when it is built with the switch on. The target's model state from #61868 then builds the draft's executor right after the target's, on the same fused kernel, mailbox and mHC side stream, and the draft model's forward asks it for a step the same way (`plan()`, then `run()`). Once the executor is built, the draft model replaces its `sample_sequential` (#64442's `FusedMarkovSampler`, which the switch implies) with one that sends batches of up to 8 request rows to the sharded chain and the others to the fused loop. `DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential` already asks that hook first, so the speculator is unchanged.

**Sharded chain: rank lockstep.**
- The chain exchanges each position's winner between ranks through a symmetric-memory mailbox, a cross-rank spin inside the draft step and its FULL graph, so every rank must launch it the same number of times.
- Whether it is installed depends only on configuration, and CPU all-reduces at load make the ranks agree on it.
- The per-call choice depends only on the padded batch shape. It applies up to 8 request rows (4 at 8 ranks).
- Steady state reads nothing back from the GPU.
- The draws reproduce the speculator's `gumbel_sample` loop, except for the bias reduction order before its BF16 rounding, so a bias element can differ from cuBLAS's in its last bit. The fused loop above 8 rows draws by inverse CDF (#64442); both sample the cached draft distribution exactly.

## Changelog

- 10-15: First version, stacked on #61868. The draft layers then moved into a draft executor, following #61867.
- 10-17: The draft finalize and the sharded Markov chain ported from run-time-compiled CUDA to CuTe DSL, with bitwise-identical outputs. Rebased onto `main` `03ee2e13` (FlashInfer 0.7.2).
- 10-19 and 10-20: Rebased onto `main` `aa3564ce` and `3b518982`.
- 10-21: #61868 merged; `main` merged into this branch.
- 11-03: Following review, dropped every change outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`: the post-forward CUDA graph, the context side stream, the multi-group DFlash prepare and the generic fused Markov sampler. The draft now samples through the existing `sample_sequential` hook, on #64442's fused loop, and the sharded chain moved to `specialized_decode/sampling/`. Merged `main` `866bccf0` (the measurements above), then `1fc9d008`.

+multiply-adds and slots whose permuted row is -1 skipped. This is the
+arithmetic of FlashInfer's TRT-LLM-gen finalize kernel for small batches (one

+            [Float32(v).ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip) for v in (a, b, c)],

+            is_align_stack=False,

+"""The specialized decode of the DSpark draft model.
+
+With DSpark speculative decoding, a few extra DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder layers
+(``DSparkDeepseekV4Model``) draft the next tokens from the target's hidden
+states after every target step, in CUDA graphs of their own. ``DraftDecode``
+runs those layers for the FULL-graph pure decode steps, as ``SpecializedDecode``
+runs the target's, through the same per-layer steps and on the kernels and
+streams the target's executor owns: the fused all-reduce + mHC kernel and its
+Lamport mailbox, the publishing ``wo_b`` GEMM and the mHC side stream. The
+draft runs between target steps on the same stream, so sharing them needs no
+synchronization beyond the stream order.
+
+The draft's layers differ from the target's in ways the steps take as
+parameters:
+
+- the first layer takes ``[n, hc, H]`` streams, the embedding expanded to the
+  hc copies, through its own mHC pre (``Boundaries.first``);
+- the layers are built as stock layers, which reduce ``wo_b`` and the MoE
+  themselves; ``AttentionStep`` projects ``wo_b`` without that all-reduce and
+  ``MoEStep`` runs the runner's body, so both stay TP-partial for the next
+  boundary's fused kernel;
+- each layer finalizes its MoE (the fused kernel's finalize is built for the
+  target's top-k): up to ``LOW_BATCH_MAX_ROWS`` rows on the low-batch GEMMs,
+  without the target's fused front, and the finalize kernel;
+- the last boundary reduces that plain tensor in the fused kernel's
+  residual-only variant, and the streams are collapsed with the last pre-mix,
+  before the final norm, which ``compute_logits`` applies.
+
+The layers are sliding-window only: they share each SWA KV-cache group's
+sparse-index table (``SparseIndexTables``), and the sparse MLA keeps the stock
+decode's wide non-causal window of the draft tokens.
+
+The target's model state builds this executor after the target's, on every TP
+rank in the same order, and warms its GEMMs up with the target's. Every
+forward that ``plan`` refuses runs the stock layers.
+"""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, NamedTuple, cast
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.forward_context import is_forward_context_available
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.mhc.triton import hc_collapse_triton
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.query_quant import can_fuse_query_quant

+from ..attention.sparse_mla import SparseIndexTables, SparseMlaDecode
+from ..attention.step import AttentionStep
+from ..boundary.boundary import BoundaryState
+from ..moe.routed_expert_gemm import build_routed_expert_gemms

+from .decode import (
+    DecodeStep,
+    SpecializedDecode,
+    captures_pure_decode,
+    flashinfer_attentions,
+    step_gates,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from ...dspark import DSparkDeepseekV4Model
+    from ...model import DeepseekV4DecoderLayer
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+def check_low_batch_graph(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> None:
+    """Log when no DSpark draft CUDA graph is small enough for the low-batch
+    GEMMs: the drafter rounds each capture size up to whole requests, so a
+    one-request graph needs a capture size of one request's draft rows."""
+    spec = vllm_config.speculative_config
+    sizes = vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes
+    if spec is None or not sizes:
+        return
+    sample_from_anchor = getattr(
+        spec.draft_model_config.hf_config, "sample_from_anchor", True
+    )
+    rows = spec.num_speculative_tokens + (0 if sample_from_anchor else 1)
+    smallest = min(-(-size // rows) * rows for size in sizes)
+    if smallest > LOW_BATCH_MAX_ROWS:
+        logger.info_once(
+            "The smallest DSpark draft CUDA graph has %d rows, so the draft "
+            "layers never take the low-batch GEMMs; add %d to "
+            "cudagraph_capture_sizes for a one-request draft graph.",
+            smallest,
+            rows,
+        )
+
+
+class DraftLayerPlan(NamedTuple):
+    layer: "DeepseekV4DecoderLayer"
+    attention: AttentionStep
+    moe: MoEStep
+
+
+class DraftDecode:
+    """The decode executor over the DSpark draft model's layers."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, target: SpecializedDecode, backbone: "DSparkDeepseekV4Model"
+    ) -> None:
+        if backbone.use_sequence_parallel or backbone.use_native_mega_moe:

+                "decode_backend=latency_specialized runs the DSpark draft without "
+                "sequence parallelism or the native mega MoE"

+        attns = flashinfer_attentions(layers)
+        self.mhc_stream = target.mhc_stream
+        self.all_reduce = target.all_reduce
+        self.boundaries = target.boundaries
+        self.tables = SparseIndexTables(attns)
+        # The persistent KV counters are the target's: the draft's decode
+        # launches run after the target's on the same stream.

+            self.tables, FUSED_MHC_MAX_ROWS * max(attn.padded_heads for attn in attns)

+        gemms = build_routed_expert_gemms(
+            [layer.ffn.experts for layer in layers], fused_front=False

+        quantize = self.all_reduce.quantize_layer_input

+            DraftLayerPlan(
+                layer=layer,
+                attention=AttentionStep(
+                    attn,
+                    self.tables,
+                    self.mla,
+                    target.publisher,
+                    mxfp8_input=quantize and can_fuse_query_quant([attn.fused_wqa_wkv]),
+                    source=None,
+                    consumer=None,
+                ),
+                moe=MoEStep(layer.ffn, gemm, FUSED_MHC_MAX_ROWS, finalize=True),
+            )
+            for layer, attn, gemm in zip(layers, attns, gemms)
+        ]
+        self._swa_prefixes = sorted({attn.swa_cache_layer.prefix for attn in attns})
+
+    def plan(self, positions: torch.Tensor) -> DecodeStep | None:
+        """The step this forward runs, or None to run the stock layers: as for
+        the target, only FULL CUDA graph captures of pure decode steps of up to
+        ``FUSED_MHC_MAX_ROWS`` rows run the executor."""
+        rows = positions.shape[0]
+        if (
+            not 0 < rows <= FUSED_MHC_MAX_ROWS
+            or not is_forward_context_available()
+            or not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+            or not captures_pure_decode(self._swa_prefixes)
+        ):
+            return None
+        return step_gates(rows, self)
+
+    def run(
+        self,
+        step: DecodeStep,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        engram_hashes: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        engram_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """The draft layers and the collapse of the step on the hc streams
+        ``x`` ([n, hc, H]); returns the pre-norm hidden state, as
+        ``DSparkDeepseekV4Model.forward`` does. The draft has no Engram
+        layers, so ``engram_hashes`` and ``engram_mask`` stay None."""
+        assert engram_hashes is None and engram_mask is None
+        bound = self.boundaries
+        self.tables.reset()
+        self.all_reduce.reset()
+        state: BoundaryState | None = None
+        try:
+            for plan in self.plans:
+                quant = None
+                if state is None:
+                    state, layer_input = bound.first(plan.layer, x, step)
+                else:
+                    state, layer_input, quant, _ = bound.sublayer(
+                        plan.layer,
+                        False,
+                        state,
+                        step,
+                        quantize=plan.attention.mxfp8_input,
+                    )
+                state.pending = plan.attention.run(layer_input, quant, positions, step)
+                bound.join(step)
+                state, ffn_input, _, _ = bound.sublayer(plan.layer, True, state, step)
+                state.pending = plan.moe.run(ffn_input, input_ids, step)
+                bound.join(step)
+            assert state is not None
+            # No successor boundary: reduce the last layer's output into the
+            # streams only.
+            streams = bound.post_only(state, fuse_partial=True)
+        except BaseException:
+            # Rejoin so that a capture reports this error, not unjoined work.
+            self.tables.join()
+            torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(self.mhc_stream)
+            raise
+        self.tables.join()
+        return hc_collapse_triton(streams, state.pre)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""DSpark Markov sampling with the Markov head sharded by vocabulary.
+
+After the DSpark backbone produces the base logits of its ``N`` draft
+positions, the draft tokens are drawn one position at a time: the bias
+``markov_head @ markov_embed[previous token]`` (``[V, r]`` by ``[r]``; 66 MB of
+BF16 for DeepSeek-V4.1) is added to the position's logits and the token is
+sampled from the result. The speculator's loop runs a replicated bias GEMM and
+its sampling kernels per position, so every tensor-parallel rank streams the
+whole head ``N`` times.
+
+Here one cooperative kernel per rank (``sharded_markov_cute.py``, CuTe DSL)
+runs the whole chain. Rank ``k`` of ``world`` owns rows
+``[k V / world, (k + 1) V / world)`` of the head and keeps them in registers
+for the launch, so the head is read once; the ranks agree on each position's
+winner by exchanging one 64-bit ``(score, index)`` key per rank, request row
+and position through a mailbox in symmetric memory. A call samples up to 8
+request rows (4 with 8 ranks), the columns of the tensor-core MMA. Padding rows
+(negative request-state index) are inert, as in the speculator's loop.
+
+Per call::
+
+    Triton noise kernel   gumbel[i, v] of this rank's vocabulary shard
+          |               (``gumbel_sample``'s hash), drawn on a side
+          v               stream while the draft LM head runs
+    chain kernel, step i  logit = cache_round(base + bf16(head . embed[p]))
+                          local cache and every peer's staging <- logit
+                          key = max over the shard of (logit / T + gumbel, index)
+                          mailbox exchange -> winner p = draft_tokens[i]
+    chain kernel, tail    cache <- the peers' shards from the local staging
+
+The draws reproduce the speculator's ``gumbel_sample`` loop (same noise,
+rounding, temperature division and ``torch.argmax`` tie-breaking) except for
+the bias reduction order before its BF16 rounding, so a bias element can differ
+from cuBLAS's in its last bit.
+
+With ``decode_backend=latency_specialized``, the DSpark draft model's
+``sample_sequential`` (the hook ``DSparkSpeculator._sample_sequential`` asks
+first) is a ``ShardedMarkovSampling``: batches of up to ``max_rows`` request
+rows take this chain, larger ones the fused loop of ``ops/fused_markov.py``.
+
+The exchange is a cross-rank spin wait inside the draft step (and its FULL
+CUDA graph): every rank must launch the kernel the same number of times.
+Installation depends on configuration only and is agreed across the group, and
+the per-call choice depends only on the padded batch shape, which tensor
+parallelism keeps identical across ranks; a rank that diverges hangs.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from functools import cache
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+from torch.distributed import ProcessGroup
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dspark.speculator import DSparkSpeculator
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.gumbel import (
+    _DRAFT_NOISE_SALT,
+    _log1p_neg_stable,
+    murmur3_uniform32,
+    spec_step_seed,
+)
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+RANK_DIM = 256
+WARPS = 16  # per CTA (sharded_markov_cute.py)
+MAX_STEPS = 8
+MAX_RANKS = 8
+MAX_ROWS = 8  # MMA columns
+MAX_VOCAB = (1 << 17) - 1  # the candidate key's index field
+STAGING_OFFSET = 16384  # bytes; the mailbox records come first
+CONTROL_WORDS = 256  # int32 control words (sharded_markov_cute.py)
+NOISE_BLOCK = 1024
+DTYPES = (torch.bfloat16, torch.float32)  # base logits and cache
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _shard_noise_kernel(
+    noise_ptr,
+    idx_mapping_ptr,
+    sample_pos_ptr,
+    seeds_ptr,
+    vocab_offset,
+    vocab_local,
+    num_steps,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Draft Gumbel noise of this rank's vocabulary shard for one (request row,
+    position), as ``gumbel_noised_argmax`` draws it (fp32, drafting salt) with
+    the draft step mixed into the seed. Samples are ordered (row, step)."""
+    sample = tl.program_id(0)
+    cols = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = cols < vocab_local
+    req_state_idx = tl.load(idx_mapping_ptr + sample).to(tl.int64)
+    is_valid_req = req_state_idx >= 0
+    seed = tl.load(seeds_ptr + req_state_idx, mask=is_valid_req, other=0)
+    seed = spec_step_seed(seed, sample % num_steps)
+    pos = tl.load(sample_pos_ptr + sample) - 1 + _DRAFT_NOISE_SALT
+    u = murmur3_uniform32(seed, pos, vocab_offset + cols)
+    gumbel_noise = -tl.log(-_log1p_neg_stable(u))
+    tl.store(noise_ptr + sample * vocab_local + cols, gumbel_noise, mask=mask)
+
+
+@cache
+def _kernel(
+    device_index: int, steps: int, base_dtype: torch.dtype, cache_dtype: torch.dtype
+):
+    """The CuTe DSL chain kernel compiled for a device, ``steps`` draft
+    positions and the base-logits and cache dtypes. Its 512-thread CTA fits one
+    per SM, and a call never launches more CTAs than the device has SMs, so the
+    cooperative grid is always co-resident."""
+    import cutlass
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cutlass import Int32, Int64
+    from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream
+
+    from .sharded_markov_cute import ShardedMarkovSample
+
+    types = {torch.bfloat16: cutlass.BFloat16, torch.float32: cutlass.Float32}
+    address = Int64(0)
+    with torch.accelerator.device_index(device_index):
+        return cute.compile(
+            ShardedMarkovSample(steps, types[base_dtype], types[cache_dtype]),
+            *[address] * 7,
+            Int32(1),
+            *[address] * 10,
+            *[Int32(1)] * 5,
+            address,
+            Int32(1),
+            make_fake_stream(),
+        )
+
+
+def _all_ranks_true(group: ProcessGroup | None, value: bool) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``value`` holds on every rank of ``group`` (CPU collective)."""
+    if group is None:
+        return value
+    flag = torch.tensor([int(value)], dtype=torch.int32)
+    dist.all_reduce(flag, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN, group=group)
+    return bool(flag.item())
+
+
+def unsupported_reason(
+    world: int,
+    vocab_size: int,
+    num_steps: int,
+    embed_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    head_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    cache_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> str | None:
+    """Why the sharded sampler cannot serve this configuration, or None. It
+    depends on configuration only, so every rank reaches the same answer."""
+    if world not in (1, 2, 4, MAX_RANKS):
+        return f"a tensor-parallel size of {world}"
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability(embed_weight.device) < (10, 0):
+        return "a GPU older than SM100"
+    if not 1 <= num_steps <= MAX_STEPS:
+        return f"{num_steps} draft positions"
+    if vocab_size > MAX_VOCAB or vocab_size % (16 * world) != 0:
+        return f"a vocabulary of {vocab_size} for {world} ranks"
+    if cache_dtype not in DTYPES:
+        return f"a {cache_dtype} draft-logits cache"
+    if vocab_size // world * cache_dtype.itemsize % 16 != 0:
+        return "a vocabulary shard that is not 16-byte aligned"
+    for name, weight in (("embedding", embed_weight), ("head", head_weight)):
+        if (
+            weight.dim() != 2
+            or weight.shape[0] < vocab_size
+            or weight.shape[1] != RANK_DIM
+            or weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+            or not weight.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            return f"a Markov {name} that is not contiguous BF16 [V, {RANK_DIM}]"
+    return None
+
+
+class DSparkShardedMarkovSampler:
+    """Persistent buffers, peer mappings and launchers of the sharded chain.
+
+    ``embed_weight`` ``[V, 256]`` and the replicated ``head_weight``
+    ``[V, 256]`` are BF16; this rank keeps a view of its head rows. ``group``
+    is the CPU group of the tensor-parallel ranks (None for one rank).
+    ``timeout_ms`` bounds every cross-rank wait with a trap (0: no bound, a
+    debugging aid). Batches of up to ``max_rows`` request rows, CUDA-graph
+    padding included, take the sharded chain.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        embed_weight: torch.Tensor,
+        head_weight: torch.Tensor,
+        vocab_size: int,
+        num_steps: int,
+        cache_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        group: ProcessGroup | None,
+        max_num_reqs: int,
+        timeout_ms: int = 0,
+    ):
+        device = embed_weight.device
+        self.group = group
+        self.rank = dist.get_rank(group) if group is not None else 0
+        self.world = dist.get_world_size(group) if group is not None else 1
+        reason = unsupported_reason(
+            self.world, vocab_size, num_steps, embed_weight, head_weight, cache_dtype
+        )
+        if reason is not None:
+            raise ValueError(f"sharded Markov sampling does not support {reason}")
+        self.device = device
+        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
+        self.num_steps = num_steps
+        self.cache_dtype = cache_dtype
+        self.timeout_ns = int(timeout_ms) * 1_000_000
+        self.vocab_local = vocab_size // self.world
+        self.vocab_offset = self.rank * self.vocab_local
+        self.embed_weight = embed_weight
+        self.head_shard = head_weight[
+            self.vocab_offset : self.vocab_offset + self.vocab_local
+        ]
+        self.ctas = min(
+            torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).multi_processor_count,
+            triton.cdiv(self.vocab_local // 16, WARPS),
+        )
+        # The exchange gives each (request row, rank) pair one lane of a warp.
+        self.max_rows = max(1, min(MAX_ROWS, 32 // self.world, max_num_reqs))
+        self.noise = torch.empty(
+            self.max_rows * num_steps,
+            self.vocab_local,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device=device,
+        )
+        self.control = torch.zeros(CONTROL_WORDS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        # Compile before the collective set-up, so that a build failure cannot
+        # leave peers waiting, and before any CUDA graph capture.
+        index = device.index
+        self.device_index = (
+            torch.accelerator.current_device_index() if index is None else index
+        )
+        failure = None
+        try:
+            for base_dtype in DTYPES:
+                _kernel(self.device_index, num_steps, base_dtype, cache_dtype)
+        except Exception as error:  # any compile failure is agreed on below
+            failure = error
+        if not _all_ranks_true(group, failure is None):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"kernel set-up failed: {failure or 'on another rank'}")
+        # Mailbox records, then the staging logits of two launch parities.
+        size = STAGING_OFFSET + (
+            2 * self.max_rows * num_steps * vocab_size * cache_dtype.itemsize
+        )
+        self._peer_buffer, peer_pointers = self._allocate_peer_buffer(size)
+        self.peers = torch.tensor(peer_pointers, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        self._noise_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device)
+
+    def _allocate_peer_buffer(self, size: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, list[int]]:
+        """The zeroed mailbox and staging buffer and every rank's mapping of it
+        (symmetric memory for more than one rank)."""
+        if self.group is None:
+            buffer = torch.zeros(size, dtype=torch.uint8, device=self.device)
+            return buffer, [buffer.data_ptr()]
+        import torch.distributed._symmetric_memory as symm_mem
+
+        # The rendezvous is collective: agree on the allocation first, so that
+        # a rank that failed it cannot leave its peers waiting there.
+        buffer = None

+the element types of the base logits and of the draft-logits cache (BF16 or

+For request ``r``, step ``i`` needs r's previous token ``p`` (its anchor for
+``i = 0``)::

+    logits_ri = cache_round(base_ri + bf16(markov_head . markov_embed[p]))
+    d_r,i+1   = argmax(logits_ri)                     (temperature 0)
+              = argmax(logits_ri / T_r + gumbel_ri)   (otherwise)
+
+Each rank owns rows ``[rank * V/world, (rank + 1) * V/world)`` of the head.
+Each warp keeps one 16-row tile of that shard in registers for all steps, so
+the head is read once per launch; the ``m16n8k16`` MMA's eight columns carry the
+eight request rows' embeddings, so every row's bias comes from the same MMAs.
+A step is those MMAs, a CTA reduction and a two-level exchange of 64-bit
+candidate keys per request row: the CTAs of a rank fold their best key into a
+rank-local maximum, the last CTA to arrive stores that key, tagged with the
+launch epoch, into every rank's mailbox, and every CTA waits for the ``world``
+records of each row in its own mailbox and takes their maximum. The exchange is
+the grid barrier and the cross-rank argmax at once, so the grid must be
+co-resident: the kernel is launched cooperatively, and its 512-thread
+requirement keeps one CTA per SM within the register file.

+draft LM head's output before its all-gather): ``base_column`` is the column of
+this rank's first vocabulary entry in them, ``rank * V/world`` or 0.

+in the speculator's loop: their tokens are drawn greedily and their logits are

+writes its shard into its own cache and into a staging buffer of every peer;
+after the last exchange each rank copies the peers' shards from its staging

+parities so that a launch never overwrites what a peer may still be reading
+from the previous launch.

+            "=f,f",
+            False,
+            loc,
+            ip,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+@dsl_user_op
+def float_bits(value, *, loc=None, ip=None) -> Uint32:
+    """The bits of an FP32 value."""
+    return Uint32(
+        _asm(
+            T.i32(),
+            _values([Float32(value)], loc, ip),
+            "mov.b32 $0, $1;",
+            "=r,f",
+            False,
+            loc,
+            ip,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def candidate_key(score: Float32, index: Int32) -> Uint64:
+    """[48:17] order-preserving score bits, [16:0] inverted index (ties prefer
+    the smaller index, as ``torch.argmax`` does). Larger is better; 0 means "no
+    key"."""
+    bits = float_bits(score)
+    ordered = bits | Uint32(0x80000000)
+    if bits & Uint32(0x80000000) != Uint32(0):
+        ordered = bits ^ Uint32(0xFFFFFFFF)
+    return (Uint64(ordered) << INDEX_BITS) | Uint64(Uint32(INDEX_MASK) - Uint32(index))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def key_index(key: Uint64) -> Int32:
+    """The vocabulary index of a candidate key."""
+    return Int32(Uint32(INDEX_MASK) - (Uint32(key) & Uint32(INDEX_MASK)))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def shuffle_xor_u64(value: Uint64, offset: Int32) -> Uint64:
+    """``__shfl_xor_sync`` of a 64-bit value over the full warp."""
+    lo = cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(Uint32(value), offset)
+    hi = cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(Uint32(value >> 32), offset)
+    return (Uint64(Uint32(hi)) << 32) | Uint64(Uint32(lo))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def shuffle_idx_u64(value: Uint64, source: Int32) -> Uint64:
+    """``__shfl_sync`` of a 64-bit value from lane ``source``."""
+    lo = cute.arch.shuffle_sync(Uint32(value), source)
+    hi = cute.arch.shuffle_sync(Uint32(value >> 32), source)
+    return (Uint64(Uint32(hi)) << 32) | Uint64(Uint32(lo))
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def max_u64(a: Uint64, b: Uint64) -> Uint64:
+    """The larger of two keys (unsigned; tensor loads come back signed)."""
+    result = Uint64(a)
+    other = Uint64(b)
+    if other > result:
+        result = other
+    return result
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def await_record(
+    address: Int64, tag: Uint32, timeout_ns: Int64, step: Int32, source: Int32
+) -> Uint64:
+    """Spin until the mailbox record at ``address`` carries ``tag``; return
+    its key. With a positive ``timeout_ns`` a wait that exceeds it reports and
+    traps instead of hanging (debug aid for ranks that disagree on the launch
+    sequence)."""
+    value = load_scalar(address, "ld.relaxed.sys.global.u64", Uint64, True)
+    if Uint32(value) & Uint32(TAG_MASK) != tag:
+        start = Int64(0)
+        if timeout_ns > 0:
+            start = cute.arch.globaltimer()
+        spins = Uint32(0)
+        while Uint32(value) & Uint32(TAG_MASK) != tag:
+            value = load_scalar(address, "ld.relaxed.sys.global.u64", Uint64, True)
+            spins = spins + Uint32(1)
+            if timeout_ns > 0 and spins & Uint32(1023) == Uint32(0):
+                waited = cute.arch.globaltimer() - start
+                if waited > timeout_ns:
+                    cute.printf(
+                        "sharded Markov sampler: step {} waited {} ns for rank {} "
+                        "(tag {}, saw {})",
+                        step,
+                        timeout_ns,
+                        source,
+                        tag,
+                        Uint32(value) & Uint32(TAG_MASK),
+                    )
+                    trap()
+    return value >> TAG_BITS
+
+
+class ShardedMarkovSample:
+    """The sharded Markov chain kernel for ``steps`` draft positions, base
+    logits of ``base_dtype`` and a draft-logits cache of ``cache_dtype``
+    (``cutlass.BFloat16`` or ``cutlass.Float32``)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, steps: int, base_dtype, cache_dtype):
+        assert 1 <= steps <= MAX_STEPS
+        self.steps = steps
+        self.base_bf16 = base_dtype is BFloat16
+        self.cache_dtype = cache_dtype
+        self.cache_bf16 = cache_dtype is BFloat16
+        self.cache_bytes = 2 if self.cache_bf16 else 4
+        # A 16-row tile of logits is this many 16-byte vectors of this many
+        # elements.
+        self.vector_elements = 16 // self.cache_bytes
+        self.tile_vectors = 16 // self.vector_elements
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        base_logits: Int64,  # [rows, steps, vocab or vocab_local]
+        base_row_stride: Int64,  # elements
+        base_step_stride: Int64,
+        base_column: Int64,  # column of this rank's shard
+        embed_table: Int64,  # BF16 [vocab, 256]
+        head: Int64,  # this rank's BF16 [vocab_local, 256]
+        input_ids: Int64,  # int32; row r's anchor at [r * query_per_row]
+        query_per_row: Int32,
+        idx_mapping: Int64,  # int64 [rows * steps] request-state rows
+        temperature: Int64,  # FP32 [max_num_reqs]
+        noise: Int64,  # FP32 [rows * steps, vocab_local]
+        logits_cache: Int64,  # [max_num_reqs, steps, vocab]
+        cache_stride0: Int64,
+        cache_stride1: Int64,
+        draft_tokens: Int64,  # int64 [rows, steps]
+        draft_stride: Int64,  # row stride
+        peers: Int64,  # u64 [world] peer buffer bases
+        control: Int64,  # local control words
+        rank: Int32,
+        world: Int32,
+        vocab_local: Int32,
+        rows: Int32,
+        max_rows: Int32,
+        timeout_ns: Int64,
+        ctas: Int32,
+        stream: cuda.CUstream,
+    ):
+        """Launch the chain as a cooperative grid of ``ctas`` CTAs."""
+        self.kernel(
+            base_logits,
+            base_row_stride,
+            base_step_stride,
+            base_column,
+            embed_table,
+            head,
+            input_ids,
+            query_per_row,
+            idx_mapping,
+            temperature,
+            noise,
+            logits_cache,
+            cache_stride0,
+            cache_stride1,
+            draft_tokens,
+            draft_stride,
+            peers,
+            control,
+            rank,
+            world,
+            vocab_local,
+            rows,
+            max_rows,
+            timeout_ns,
+        ).launch(
+            grid=(ctas, 1, 1), block=[THREADS, 1, 1], stream=stream, cooperative=True
+        )
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def peer_base(self, peers: Int64, peer: Int32) -> Int64:
+        """The base address of ``peer``'s buffer."""
+        return load_scalar(peers + Int64(peer) * 8, "ld.global.nc.u64", Int64)
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def load_base(
+        self,
+        base_logits: Int64,
+        row_stride: Int64,
+        step_stride: Int64,
+        column: Int64,
+        r: Int32,
+        step: Int32,
+        row: Int32,
+    ) -> Float32:
+        """Base logit of request row ``r``, ``step`` and shard row ``row``."""
+        element = (
+            Int64(r) * row_stride + Int64(step) * step_stride + column + Int64(row)
+        )
+        value = Float32(0.0)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(self.base_bf16):
+            value = load_bf16_as_f32(base_logits + element * 2)
+        else:
+            value = load_scalar(base_logits + element * 4, "ld.global.f32", Float32)
+        return value
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def load_noise(
+        self, noise: Int64, r: Int32, step: Int32, row: Int32, vocab_local: Int32
+    ) -> Float32:
+        """Gumbel noise of request row ``r``, ``step`` and shard row ``row``."""
+        element = Int64(r * self.steps + step) * Int64(vocab_local) + Int64(row)
+        return load_scalar(noise + element * 4, "ld.global.f32", Float32)
+
+    @cute.jit
+    def load_inputs(
+        self,
+        base: cute.Tensor,
+        gumbel: cute.Tensor,
+        step: Int32,
+        tile: Int32,
+        g: Int32,
+        t: Int32,
+        rows: Int32,
+        base_logits: Int64,
+        row_stride: Int64,
+        step_stride: Int64,
+        column: Int64,
+        noise: Int64,
+        vocab_local: Int32,
+    ):
+        """Base logits and noise of this lane's resident tile rows and request
+        rows for ``step``: ``base``/``gumbel`` [col * 2 + half]."""
+        for col in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+            r = 2 * t + col
+            if r < rows:
+                for half in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                    row = tile * 16 + g + 8 * half
+                    base[col * 2 + half] = self.load_base(
+                        base_logits, row_stride, step_stride, column, r, step, row
+                    )
+                    gumbel[col * 2 + half] = self.load_noise(
+                        noise, r, step, row, vocab_local
+                    )
+
+    @cute.kernel
+    def kernel(
+        self,
+        base_logits: Int64,
+        base_row_stride: Int64,
+        base_step_stride: Int64,
+        base_column: Int64,
+        embed_table: Int64,
+        head: Int64,
+        input_ids: Int64,
+        query_per_row: Int32,
+        idx_mapping: Int64,
+        temperature: Int64,
+        noise: Int64,
+        logits_cache: Int64,
+        cache_stride0: Int64,
+        cache_stride1: Int64,
+        draft_tokens: Int64,
+        draft_stride: Int64,
+        peers: Int64,
+        control: Int64,
+        rank: Int32,
+        world: Int32,
+        vocab_local: Int32,
+        rows: Int32,
+        max_rows: Int32,
+        timeout_ns: Int64,
+    ):
+        """One CTA of 16 warps; see the module docstring."""
+        steps = self.steps
+        cache_bytes = self.cache_bytes
+        vector_elements = self.vector_elements
+        tile_vectors = self.tile_vectors
+
+        @cute.struct
+        class Shared:
+            embedding: cute.struct.Align[
+                cute.struct.MemRange[Uint32, MAX_ROWS * RANK_DIM // 2], 16
+            ]
+            tile_logits: cute.struct.Align[
+                cute.struct.MemRange[Uint32, WARPS * MAX_ROWS * 16 * cache_bytes // 4],
+                16,
+            ]
+            warp_best: cute.struct.MemRange[Uint64, WARPS * MAX_ROWS]
+            winner: cute.struct.MemRange[Uint64, MAX_ROWS]
+            count: cute.struct.MemRange[Uint32, 1]
+
+        shared = cutlass.utils.SmemAllocator().allocate(Shared)
+        embedding = shared_address(shared.embedding.data_ptr())
+        tile_words = shared.tile_logits.data_ptr()
+        tile_base = shared_address(tile_words)
+        tile_logits = cute.make_tensor(
+            cute.recast_ptr(tile_words, dtype=self.cache_dtype),
+            cute.make_layout((WARPS, MAX_ROWS, 16), stride=(MAX_ROWS * 16, 16, 1)),
+        )
+        warp_best = cute.make_tensor(
+            shared.warp_best.data_ptr(),
+            cute.make_layout((WARPS, MAX_ROWS), stride=(MAX_ROWS, 1)),
+        )
+        winner = cute.make_tensor(shared.winner.data_ptr(), cute.make_layout(MAX_ROWS))
+        count = cute.make_tensor(shared.count.data_ptr(), cute.make_layout(1))
+
+        thread, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+        cta, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+        ctas, _, _ = cute.arch.grid_dim()
+        warp = thread // 32
+        lane = thread % 32
+        g = lane // 4
+        t = lane % 4
+        tiles = vocab_local // 16
+        stride = ctas * WARPS
+        first_tile = cta * WARPS + warp
+        vocab_offset = rank * vocab_local
+        vocab = Int64(vocab_local) * Int64(world)
+        resident = first_tile < tiles
+
+        # The resident tile: rows g and g + 8, 16 bytes at k = 32 chunk + 8 t.
+        lo = cute.make_rmem_tensor((CHUNKS * 4,), Uint32)
+        hi = cute.make_rmem_tensor((CHUNKS * 4,), Uint32)
+        if resident:
+            tile_row = head + Int64(first_tile * 16 + g) * ROW_BYTES + Int64(t * 16)
+            for chunk in cutlass.range_constexpr(CHUNKS):
+                words_lo = load_v4(tile_row + chunk * 64, "ld.global.nc.v4.u32", False)
+                words_hi = load_v4(
+                    tile_row + 8 * ROW_BYTES + chunk * 64, "ld.global.nc.v4.u32", False
+                )
+                for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+                    lo[chunk * 4 + j] = words_lo[j]
+                    hi[chunk * 4 + j] = words_hi[j]
+

+        # next step's are loaded while the exchange is in flight.
+        base = cute.make_rmem_tensor((4,), Float32)
+        gumbel = cute.make_rmem_tensor((4,), Float32)
+        base.fill(0.0)
+        gumbel.fill(0.0)
+        if resident:
+            self.load_inputs(
+                base,
+                gumbel,
+                0,
+                first_tile,
+                g,
+                t,
+                rows,
+                base_logits,
+                base_row_stride,
+                base_step_stride,
+                base_column,
+                noise,
+                vocab_local,
+            )
+
+        if thread == 0:
+            count[0] = load_scalar(
+                control + LAUNCH_WORD * 4, "ld.volatile.global.u32", Uint32, True
+            )

+        anchor_words.fill(0)

+                anchor = load_scalar(
+                    input_ids + Int64(warp * query_per_row) * 4, "ld.global.u32", Int32
+                )
+                loaded = load_v4(
+                    embed_table + Int64(anchor) * ROW_BYTES + Int64(lane * 16),
+                    "ld.global.nc.v4.u32",
+                    False,
+                )
+                for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+                    anchor_words[j] = loaded[j]
+            store_shared_v4(
+                embedding + warp * ROW_BYTES + lane * 16,
+                [anchor_words[j] for j in range(4)],

+        arrivals = control + ARRIVAL_WORD * 4

+        staging_parity = (
+            Int64(STAGING_OFFSET // cache_bytes)
+            + Int64(parity * max_rows * steps) * vocab
+        )
+
+        best = cute.make_rmem_tensor((2,), Uint64)
+        temp = cute.make_rmem_tensor((2,), Float32)
+        acc = cute.make_rmem_tensor((4,), Float32)
+        for step in cutlass.range(steps, unroll=1):
+            last_step = step + 1 == steps
+            for col in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):

+                if 2 * t + col < rows:

+                        "ld.global.u64",
+                        Int64,

+            best[1] = Uint64(0)

+                        c = mma_16816(

+                            [x[2], x[3]],

+                            stream_row + chunk * 64, "ld.global.nc.v4.u32", False
+                        )
+                        wb = load_v4(
+                            stream_row + 8 * ROW_BYTES + chunk * 64,
+                            "ld.global.nc.v4.u32",
+                            False,
+                        )
+                        d = [acc[0], acc[1], acc[2], acc[3]]
+                        d = mma_16816(d, [wa[0], wb[0], wa[1], wb[1]], [y[0], y[1]])
+                        d = mma_16816(d, [wa[2], wb[2], wa[3], wb[3]], [y[2], y[3]])

+                            acc[j] = d[j]

+                    if r < rows:
+                        for half in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                            row = tile * 16 + g + 8 * half
+                            base_value = base[col * 2 + half]
+                            noise_value = gumbel[col * 2 + half]
+                            if tile != first_tile:
+                                base_value = self.load_base(
+                                    base_logits,
+                                    base_row_stride,
+                                    base_step_stride,
+                                    base_column,
+                                    r,
+                                    step,
+                                    row,
+                                )
+                                noise_value = self.load_noise(
+                                    noise, r, step, row, vocab_local
+                                )
+                            # The bias GEMM's BF16 output, then the eager add's
+                            # FP32 sum rounded once to the cache type.
+                            bias = round_bf16(acc[2 * half + col])
+                            value = add_rn(base_value, bias)
+                            if cutlass.const_expr(self.cache_bf16):
+                                value = round_bf16(value)
+                            tile_logits[warp, r, g + 8 * half] = value.to(
+                                self.cache_dtype
+                            )
+                            score = value
+                            if temp[col] != Float32(0.0):
+                                score = add_rn(div_full(value, temp[col]), noise_value)
+                            best[col] = max_u64(
+                                best[col], candidate_key(score, vocab_offset + row)
+                            )
+                # The tile's logits leave as 16-byte vectors: one per lane and
+                # request row for the local cache and for each peer's staging
+                # buffer.
+                cute.arch.sync_warp()
+                if lane < rows * tile_vectors:
+                    vec_row = lane // tile_vectors
+                    vec = lane - vec_row * tile_vectors
+                    vec_state = load_scalar(
+                        idx_mapping + Int64(vec_row * steps + step) * 8,
+                        "ld.global.u64",
+                        Int64,
+                    )
+                    if vec_state >= 0:
+                        packed = load_shared_v4(
+                            tile_base
+                            + (warp * MAX_ROWS + vec_row) * 16 * cache_bytes
+                            + vec * 16
+                        )
+                        element = Int64(
+                            vocab_offset + tile * 16 + vec * vector_elements
+                        )
+                        store_global_v4(
+                            logits_cache
+                            + (
+                                vec_state * cache_stride0
+                                + Int64(step) * cache_stride1
+                                + element
+                            )
+                            * cache_bytes,
+                            packed,
+                        )
+                        staged = (
+                            staging_parity
+                            + Int64(vec_row * steps + step) * vocab
+                            + element
+                        ) * cache_bytes
+                        for peer in cutlass.range(world, unroll=1):
+                            if peer != rank:
+                                store_global_v4(
+                                    self.peer_base(peers, peer) + staged, packed
+                                )
+                cute.arch.sync_warp()
+            if step + 1 < steps and resident:
+                self.load_inputs(
+                    base,
+                    gumbel,
+                    step + 1,
+                    first_tile,
+                    g,
+                    t,
+                    rows,
+                    base_logits,
+                    base_row_stride,
+                    base_step_stride,
+                    base_column,
+                    noise,
+                    vocab_local,
+                )
+
+            # Each request row's best key over the warp (lanes sharing t), then
+            # the CTA.
+            for col in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                for level in cutlass.range_constexpr(3):
+                    best[col] = max_u64(
+                        best[col], shuffle_xor_u64(best[col], 4 << level)
+                    )
+            if g == 0:
+                warp_best[warp, 2 * t] = best[0]
+                warp_best[warp, 2 * t + 1] = best[1]
+            cute.arch.sync_threads()
+            if warp == 0:
+                if lane < rows:
+                    key = Uint64(0)
+                    for w in cutlass.range_constexpr(WARPS):
+                        key = max_u64(key, warp_best[w, lane])
+                    atomic(
+                        control + Int64(step * MAX_ROWS + lane) * 8,
+                        key,
+                        "atom.global.max.u64",
+                    )
+                cute.arch.sync_warp()
+                last = Int32(0)
+                if lane == 0:
+                    # The last step's fence also publishes this CTA's peer
+                    # stores of every step before its arrival is counted.
+                    if last_step:
+                        fence("sys")
+                    else:
+                        fence("gl")
+                    arrived = atomic(
+                        arrivals + Int64(step) * 4, Uint32(1), "atom.global.add.u32"
+                    )
+                    if arrived == Uint32(ctas - 1):
+                        last = Int32(1)
+                last = cute.arch.shuffle_sync(last, 0)
+                # Lane L handles request row L / world and rank L % world.
+                ex_row = lane // world
+                other_rank = lane - ex_row * world
+                exchanging = lane < rows * world
+                # Post every row slot up to max_rows (rows past `rows` carry
+                # the zero key) so each slot is rewritten on every launch of
+                # its parity. Graphs of different row counts share the launch
+                # counter; a slot left from a larger launch could otherwise
+                # carry a tag that matches a later one.
+                posting = lane < max_rows * world
+                record = (
+                    (Int64(parity) * MAX_STEPS + Int64(step)) * MAX_ROWS + Int64(ex_row)
+                ) * MAX_RANKS
+                if last != 0:
+                    if lane == 0:
+                        fence("gl")
+                    cute.arch.sync_warp()
+                    rank_key = Uint64(0)
+                    if lane < rows:
+                        rank_key = atomic(
+                            control + Int64(step * MAX_ROWS + lane) * 8,
+                            Uint64(0),
+                            "atom.global.exch.b64",
+                        )
+                    if lane == 0:
+                        atomic(
+                            arrivals + Int64(step) * 4,
+                            Uint32(0),

+vocabulary across the tensor-parallel ranks (``sharded_markov.py`` explains the
+design). It is compiled for a number of draft positions ``steps`` (1..8) and
+the element types of the base logits and of the draft-logits cache (BF16 or
+FP32).

+``i = 0``)::
+
+    logits_ri = cache_round(base_ri + bf16(markov_head . markov_embed[p]))
+    d_r,i+1   = argmax(logits_ri)                     (temperature 0)
+              = argmax(logits_ri / T_r + gumbel_ri)   (otherwise)
+
+Each rank owns rows ``[rank * V/world, (rank + 1) * V/world)`` of the head.
+Each warp keeps one 16-row tile of that shard in registers for all steps, so
+the head is read once per launch; the ``m16n8k16`` MMA's eight columns carry the
+eight request rows' embeddings, so every row's bias comes from the same MMAs.
+A step is those MMAs, a CTA reduction and a two-level exchange of 64-bit
+candidate keys per request row: the CTAs of a rank fold their best key into a
+rank-local maximum, the last CTA to arrive stores that key, tagged with the
+launch epoch, into every rank's mailbox, and every CTA waits for the ``world``
+records of each row in its own mailbox and takes their maximum. The exchange is
+the grid barrier and the cross-rank argmax at once, so the grid must be
+co-resident: the kernel is launched cooperatively, and its 512-thread
+requirement keeps one CTA per SM within the register file.
+
+The base logits may hold the full vocabulary or only this rank's shard (the
+draft LM head's output before its all-gather): ``base_column`` is the column of
+this rank's first vocabulary entry in them, ``rank * V/world`` or 0.
+
+Rows whose request-state index is negative (CUDA-graph padding) are inert, as
+in the fused path: their tokens are drawn greedily and their logits are not
+cached.
+
+The draft-logits cache must hold the full vocabulary on every rank. Each rank
+writes its shard into its own cache and into a staging buffer of every peer;
+after the last exchange each rank copies the peers' shards from its staging
+buffer into its cache. Staging and mailbox records alternate between two
+parities so that a launch never overwrites what a peer may still be reading
+from the previous launch.
+

+``[parity 2][step 8][row 8][source rank 8]`` (8 KiB), then the staging logits
+``[parity 2][max_rows][steps][vocab]`` of the cache type at ``STAGING_OFFSET``.

+0..127, arrivals ``[step 8]`` at 128..135, launches at 136, end arrivals at 137.
+
+Global memory is addressed with 64-bit integers and accessed with explicit PTX,
+so that each access has the state space, cache operator and memory ordering
+the protocol needs (relaxed system-scope mailbox records, L2-only staging
+reads, non-coherent reads of the weights).
+"""

+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+from cutlass import BFloat16, Float32, Int32, Int64, Uint32, Uint64
